# Light curtain sorting -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** Sort on a measurement rather than on two bits. The curtain reports how tall each carton is, in metres, so the threshold is yours to choose — put it on the panel's pot and you can change your mind without editing the program.

**Done when.** Cartons above your threshold go down the chute and the rest pass, and moving the pot moves the boundary with no other change. The two counters together equal what the curtain measured.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`light_curtain_sorting.st`](light_curtain_sorting.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Light curtain sorting" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/light_curtain_sorting.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   ```bash
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   (From a source checkout: `cd sidecar && python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`.
   If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add `-o host 0.0.0.0` and read the warning
   it prints.) Check the address map it prints against the table below.
3. Compile `light_curtain_sorting.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh light_curtain_sorting.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 9 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 5 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 8 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 0 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses -- and pass the port it prints:

   ```bash
   python tools/grade.py --scene light-curtain-sorting
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `belt.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `BeltFault` %IX100.0 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn, whatever it is told |  |
| `belt.rotate` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `BeltRotate` %QX100.0 | run the belt | yes |
| `diverter.extend` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `DiverterExtend` %QX100.1 | extend the pusher | yes |
| `diverter.extended` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `DiverterExtended` %IX100.1 | pusher fully out | yes |
| `diverter.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `DiverterFault` %IX100.2 | drive fault: TRUE = jammed; it freezes where it is |  |
| `diverter.retracted` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `DiverterRetracted` %IX100.3 | pusher fully back | yes |
| `emitter.emit` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `EmitterEmit` %QX100.2 | rising edge = feed one carton; hold each level well over one poll | yes |
| `height_gauge.blocked` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `HeightGaugeBlocked` %IX100.4 | light curtain: TRUE while any beam is blocked | yes |
| `height_gauge.height` | PLC reads | float | 3x0 + 3x1 | `HeightGaugeHeightHi` %IW100 + `HeightGaugeHeightLo` %IW101 -> `HeightGaugeHeight` : REAL | light curtain: height of the tallest blocked beam, m (0 when clear) | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.5 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.3 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `PanelRed` %QX100.4 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x6 | `PanelReset` %IX100.6 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press |  |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x2 + 3x3 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW102 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW103 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 0..0.5 m (starts at 0.15) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x7 | `PanelStart` %IX100.7 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x8 | `PanelStop` %IX101.0 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `short_count.count` | PLC reads | int | 3x4 + 3x5 | `ShortCountCountHi` %IW104 + `ShortCountCountLo` %IW105 -> `ShortCountCount` : DINT | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total | yes |
| `tall_count.count` | PLC reads | int | 3x6 + 3x7 | `TallCountCountHi` %IW106 + `TallCountCountLo` %IW107 -> `TallCountCount` : DINT | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total | yes |

## Three things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 4:
  `height_gauge.height`, `panel.setpoint`, `short_count.count`,
  `tall_count.count`. The program's first and last sections move them between
  the registers and plain DINT/REAL variables, so your logic never sees a
  register. OpenPLC's `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the *number* (`16#3F800000`
  becomes 1065353216.0, not 1.0), so the starter rebuilds a REAL bit by bit
  instead. [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh) compiles the helpers
  with OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button click in the 3D scene holds its tag for 0.2 s (the
  panel's Press Hold setting) and then leaves it off for at least as long, so
  every click is read several times: act on its rising edge, not its level.
  The grader holds each press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an
  output you want the scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
